source_text:
Μὴ τοίνυν θεὸς ἀπὸ
γάμου καὶ φθορᾶς συλλαμ βάνεται, καὶ ἐξ ἀνδρὸς καὶ κοίτης τεχθῆναι ἢ σαρκωθῆναι

2
δύ ναται; Οὐδαμῶς, ἀλλ' ἐξ ἐνεργείας θεοῦ, ἐξ ἐπιφοιτήσεως ὑψί στου, ἐκ παρουσίας
Πνεύματος.
5 Τοιγαροῦν ἡνίκα ἡ παρθένος πρὸς τὸν Γαβριὴλ ἔλεγε· «Πῶς ἔσται μοι
τοῦτο, ἐπεὶ ἄνδρα οὐ γινώσκω;» τουτέστιν· «Ἐκ πλήττει με τὸ θαῦμα, καταπλήττει
με τὸ ῥῆμα», καὶ ὁ τοῦ ἀγ γέλου χρηματισμὸς τὴν παρθένον ἐξίστησιν. «Θαυμαστὰ
λέγεις, ἐμοὶ δὲ διὰ τὸ ξένον ὕποπτα. ∆έδοικα τοῦ εὐαγγελισμοῦ τὸ και νόν,
θορυβοῦμαι πρὸς τὸ λίαν τῶν λεγομένων ἄηθες. "3Πῶς ἔσται μοι τοῦτο, ἐπεὶ ἄνδρα
οὐ γινώσκω;"3 Πῶς ἔσομαι μή-τηρ, μὴ γενομένη νύμφη; Οὐκ ἔφθειρα τὸ τῆς ὥρας
ἄνθος, τὸν ζωστῆρα τῆς παρθενίας οὐκ ἔλυσα, τὸν δεσμὸν τῆς μήτρας οὐκ
ἐχαύνωσα, τὴν σφραγῖδα τῆς γαστρὸς οὐ παρέλυσα.» Ὁ δὲ ἄγγελος παραχρῆμα
ἐπήγαγε· «Πνεῦμα ἅγιον ἐπελεύσεται ἐπὶ σέ, καὶ δύναμις ὑψίστου ἐπισκιάσει σοι»
τουτέστιν· «Εἰ ἐγίνωσκες ἄνδρα, οὐκ ἂν ἔτεκες θεόν, δούλου μορφὴν λαβεῖν ἐκ σοῦ
διὰ σὲ χωρὶς φθορᾶς εὐδοκήσαντα, οὐκ ἂν ὄργανον ἐγένου τῆς τοῦ πάντα
παραγαγόντος σαρκώσεως. Ἀλλ' ἐπειδὴ καθαρὰ τυγχάνεις κοίτης γαμικῆς, ἐπειδὴ
τὸν ναὸν ἄφθαρτον καὶ τὴν σκηνὴν ῥύπου παντὸς ἐλευθέραν ἐτήρησας, καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ
ἐπιδημεῖ σοι καὶ τὸ Πνεῦμα ἐπισκιάζει καὶ μετὰ σαρκὸς ἐκ σοῦ ὁ Μονογενὴς τίκτεται.
Σὺ οὖν μηδαμῶς διακριθῇς τὰ ἑξῆς μυστήρια, μὴ διακριθῇς ἐν σπηλαίῳ τίκτουσα τὸν
ὅλης τῆς κτίσεως δημιουργόν, μὴ διακριθῇς ἐν φάτνῃ καθίζουσα τὸν ἐπὶ τῶν νώτων
τῶν χερουβὶμ καθεζόμενον, οὐκ ἔχουσα τόπον ἐν τῷ καταλύματι καὶ μήτηρ
βασιλέως τῶν ἄνω καὶ τῶν κάτω τυγχάνουσα.»
6 Ἑκὼν γὰρ ἐκ σοῦ πτωχεύει, ἵνα καὶ τοὺς πλουσίους χαλι-νώσῃ, καὶ τοῖς
πτωχοῖς ὑπόθεσις ὑπομονῆς καὶ διδάσκαλος εὐχαριστίας γένηται. Ἑκὼν ἐπὶ τῆς
φάτνης τίθεται, ἵνα οἱ κτηνώδεις προσδράμωσι καὶ τὸν Λόγον εὕρωσιν ἐπὶ τῆς
φάτνης καθήμενον, ἵνα ἀναλάβωσιν ἐξ αὐτοῦ τὸ λογικὸν ἀξίωμα, ἵνα σῖτον εὕρωσι
προσδοκήσαντες ἄχυρα, ἵνα ὡς κτήνη προσδράμωσι δράγματα κριθῆς ἐπὶ τῆς φάτνης
εὑρεῖν οἰόμενοι καὶ τὸν ἄρτον τὸν ἀληθινὸν φάγωσι, τὴν τροφὴν τῆς ζωῆς, τὸ
δεῖπνον τοῦ φωτός, τὴν βρῶσιν τῆς χαρᾶς, τῆς ἀφθαρσίας τὸ γλύκασμα, ἐξ οὗ τῆς
βασιλείας ἡ γνῶσις, τῆς υἱοθεσίας ὁ ἀρραβών, ὁ τῶν οὐρανῶν κλῆρος, ἡ κοινωνία
τοῦ Πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ Υἱοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος· Αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν
αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.

3
thought_title: The Virgin's Question and the Angel's Answer
orientation: Hesychius is dramatizing the dialogue between Mary and Gabriel at the Annunciation, expanding Mary's question from Luke 1:34 and Gabriel's reply from Luke 1:35 with theological commentary.
pass_a_gloss: Not then God from marriage and corruption [is] conceived, and from man and bed to be born or to be made flesh is he able? By no means, but from [the] working of God, from [the] visitation of [the] Most High, from [the] presence of [the] Spirit. Therefore when the virgin to Gabriel was saying: “How will be to me this, since man not I know?” that is: “[It] strikes me the wonder, [it] astonishes me the word,” and the of the angel response the virgin amazes. “Wonderful things you say, but to me because of the strangeness suspicious. I fear of the good news the newness, I am troubled at the very much of the things said unusual. "How will be to me this, since man not I know?" How will I be mother, not having become bride? Not I corrupted the of youth flower, the girdle of virginity not I loosed, the bond of the womb not I slackened, the seal of the belly not I loosened.” But the angel immediately brought on: “Spirit holy will come upon you, and power of [the] Most High will overshadow you” that is: “If you knew man, not would you have borne God, [the] form of a servant to take from you for you without corruption having been pleased, not would [you] have become instrument of the of the all things having brought into being incarnation. But since pure you are of bed marital, since the temple incorruptible and the tent of every filth free you kept, both the Father visits you and the Spirit overshadows and with flesh from you the Only-begotten is born. You therefore by no means doubt the next mysteries, do not doubt in cave bearing the of all creation maker, do not doubt in manger seating the upon the backs of the cherubim seated [one], not having place in the lodging and mother of [the] king of the things above and of the things below being.” Willingly for from you he becomes poor, in order that both the rich he may bridle, and to the poor [a] basis of endurance and [a] teacher of thanksgiving he may become. Willingly upon the manger he is placed, in order that the beast-like may run to [him] and the Word may find upon the manger sitting, in order that they may take up from him the rational dignity, in order that wheat they may find having expected chaff, in order that as beasts they may run to [him] sheaves of barley upon the manger to find thinking and the bread the true they may eat, the food of the life, the supper of the light, the food of the joy, of the incorruption the sweetness, from which of the kingdom the knowledge, of the adoption the pledge, the of the heavens lot, the fellowship of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit; To him [be] the glory unto the ages of the ages. Amen.

choices.term: Μὴ τοίνυν θεὸς ἀπὸ γάμου καὶ φθορᾶς συλλαμβάνεται
choices.english: Is God then conceived from marriage and corruption?
choices.why: The μή particle marks a question expecting a negative answer; rendering as a positive question preserves that force, with the following 'By no means' supplying the expected denial.
rejected: Is God not conceived from marriage and corruption?
God is not conceived from marriage and corruption.

choices.english: as you seat in a manger
choices.why: καθίζουσα is transitive here: Mary seats or places Christ in the manger; the agency is Mary's, not her sitting beside it.
rejected: as you sit by the manger

choices.why: ὑπόθεσις here means a basis or foundation for something; 'ground' captures the sense of a support or starting point for the poor's endurance.
λογικός means rational, pertaining to the Logos; ἀξίωμα is dignity or worth. The phrase plays on the Word (Λόγος) giving rational dignity to beast-like humans.
δράγμα is a handful or sheaf; barley is the coarse animal feed contrasted with the true bread.
γλύκασμα is a sweet thing or sweetness; the genitive ἀφθαρσίας is possessive, so 'of incorruption' preserves the source order and force.

bible_refs.note: Πῶς ἔσται μοι τοῦτο, ἐπεὶ ἄνδρα οὐ γινώσκω;
Πνεῦμα ἅγιον ἐπελεύσεται ἐπὶ σέ, καὶ δύναμις ὑψίστου ἐπισκιάσει σοι

pass_b_english: Is God then conceived from marriage and corruption? Can He be born or take flesh from a man and a marriage bed? By no means—but from the working of God, from the visitation of the Most High, from the presence of the Spirit.

So when the virgin said to Gabriel, “How will this be, since I do not know a man?” (Luke 1:34)—that is, “The wonder strikes me; the word overwhelms me”—the angel’s message confounds the virgin. “You say astonishing things, and because they are strange they seem suspect to me. I fear the newness of this announcement; I am troubled by how utterly unfamiliar your words are. ‘How will this be, since I do not know a man?’ How shall I become a mother without becoming a bride? I have not spoiled the flower of my youth; I have not loosed the girdle of my virginity; I have not weakened the bond of my womb; I have not undone the seal of my belly.”

But the angel immediately added, “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you” (Luke 1:35)—that is, “If you had known a man, you would not have given birth to God, who was pleased to take the form of a servant from you without corruption, for your sake; you would not have become the instrument of the incarnation of the One who brought all things into being. But since you are pure from the marriage bed, since you have kept the temple incorrupt and the tabernacle free from every stain, the Father comes to dwell with you, the Spirit overshadows you, and the Only-Begotten is born from you with flesh.

So do not doubt at all the mysteries that follow. Do not doubt as you give birth in a cave to the Creator of all creation. Do not doubt as you seat in a manger the One who sits upon the backs of the cherubim—you who have no place in the inn, and yet are the mother of the King of things above and things below.”

For willingly He becomes poor from you, so that He may bridle the rich as well, and become for the poor a ground of endurance and a teacher of thanksgiving. Willingly He is placed in the manger, so that the beast-like may run to Him and find the Word seated in the manger, so that they may receive from Him the rational dignity, so that they may find wheat when they expected chaff, so that like cattle they may run up thinking to find handfuls of barley in the manger—and may eat the true bread, the food of life, the supper of light, the nourishment of joy, the sweetness of incorruption, from which comes the knowledge of the kingdom, the pledge of adoption, the inheritance of the heavens, the communion of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit. To Him be glory forever and ever. Amen.

problems.quote: who was pleased to take the form of a servant from you for your sake without corruption
problems.source_quote: δούλου μορφὴν λαβεῖν ἐκ σοῦ διὰ σὲ χωρὶς φθορᾶς εὐδοκήσαντα
problems.why: Word order and syntax: 'from you for your sake without corruption' makes 'without corruption' ambiguous—does it modify 'take' or 'was pleased'? In Greek χωρὶς φθορᾶς clearly goes with λαβεῖν (taking flesh without corruption), but English placement after 'for your sake' makes it seem like 'was pleased without corruption', which is awkward. Also 'from you' should be closer to 'take'
problems.fix: who was pleased to take the form of a servant from you without corruption, for your sake

edits.old: who was pleased to take the form of a servant from you for your sake without corruption
edits.new: who was pleased to take the form of a servant from you without corruption, for your sake

fixed: Moved 'without corruption' next to 'take' to match the Greek χωρὶς φθορᾶς modifying λαβεῖν, and placed 'for your sake' after it.

last_rejected.quote: Is God then conceived from marriage and corruption?
last_rejected.source_quote: Μὴ τοίνυν θεὸς ἀπὸ γάμου καὶ φθορᾶς συλλαμβάνεται
last_rejected.why: Subject wrong: 'God' is subject, but Greek asks if God is conceived by marriage/corruption, not if God conceives. Passive verb 'συλλαμβάνεται' means 'is conceived,' but the agent is 'from marriage and corruption'—the question is whether God can be so conceived, not whether God does the conceiving. The English makes God the agent of conception rather than the one conceived.
last_rejected.fix: Is God then conceived by marriage and corruption? Can He be born or take flesh from a man and a marriage bed?
last_rejected.ruling: English 'Is God conceived' correctly renders passive συλλαμβάνεται; God is subject/patient, not agent. No error.

last_rejected.quote: the angel's message confounds the virgin
last_rejected.source_quote: ὁ τοῦ ἀγγέλου χρηματισμὸς τὴν παρθένον ἐξίστησιν
last_rejected.why: Wrong subject: 'χρηματισμὸς' means oracle/announcement/revelation, not 'message' in general; more importantly, the Greek says the angel's oracle 'amazes/astonishes' (ἐξίστησιν) the virgin, not 'confounds.' 'Confounds' implies confusion/defeat; ἐξίστημι here means to amaze, astonish, put outside oneself with wonder.
last_rejected.fix: the angel's oracle astonishes the virgin
last_rejected.ruling: 'Message' fits χρηματισμός; 'confounds' is within range of ἐξίστησιν (amaze/astonish). Mere preference.

last_rejected.quote: I am troubled by how utterly unfamiliar your words are
last_rejected.source_quote: θορυβοῦμαι πρὸς τὸ λίαν τῶν λεγομένων ἄηθες
last_rejected.why: Wrong syntax: 'πρὸς τὸ...ἄηθες' means 'I am troubled at the extreme unfamiliarity of what is being said,' not 'by how utterly unfamiliar your words are.' The Greek emphasizes the thing itself (τὸ ἄηθες) as cause of disturbance; 'how' is added. More seriously, 'your words' is interpretive—the Greek has 'τῶν λεγομένων' (the things being said).
last_rejected.fix: I am troubled at the extreme unfamiliarity of what is said
last_rejected.ruling: 'How utterly unfamiliar' fairly renders πρὸς τὸ λίαν ἄηθες; 'your words' for τῶν λεγομένων is natural. Mere preference.

last_rejected.quote: I have not spoiled the flower of my youth
last_rejected.source_quote: Οὐκ ἔφθειρα τὸ τῆς ὥρας ἄνθος
last_rejected.why: Wrong sense: 'ὥρα' here means 'season, prime' (especially of virginity/maidenhood), not 'youth' generally. 'Flower of my youth' loses the specific nuance of the season of maidenly prime. More importantly, 'spoiled' for ἔφθειρα is weak—'corrupted, ruined, destroyed' would be stronger. But 'spoiled' is within range. The 'youth' for ὥρα is the main issue.
last_rejected.fix: I have not corrupted the flower of my season
last_rejected.ruling: 'Youth' is within range of ὥρα; 'spoiled' fits ἔφθειρα. No meaning lost.

last_rejected.quote: I have not weakened the bond of my womb
last_rejected.source_quote: τὸν δεσμὸν τῆς μήτρας οὐκ ἐχαύνωσα
last_rejected.why: Wrong sense: 'ἐχαύνωσα' means 'softened, loosened, relaxed' (from χαυνόω), not 'weakened.' The image is of a seal or bond becoming soft/loose, not losing strength. 'Weakened' changes the physical metaphor.
last_rejected.fix: I have not loosened the bond of my womb
last_rejected.ruling: 'Weakened' is within range of ἐχαύνωσα (loosen/relax/weaken). Mere preference.

last_rejected.quote: I have not undone the seal of my belly
last_rejected.source_quote: τὴν σφραγῖδα τῆς γαστρὸς οὐ παρέλυσα
last_rejected.why: Wrong sense: 'παρέλυσα' means 'loosed, released, broke,' not 'undone.' 'Undone' is too weak and vague. 'Loosed' or 'broken' preserves the force of the physical seal being removed/broken.
last_rejected.fix: I have not loosed the seal of my belly
last_rejected.ruling: 'Undone' is within range of παρέλυσα (loosed/broke/undone). Mere preference.

last_rejected.quote: who was pleased to take the form of a servant from you without corruption, for your sake
last_rejected.source_quote: δούλου μορφὴν λαβεῖν ἐκ σοῦ διὰ σὲ χωρὶς φθορᾶς εὐδοκήσαντα
last_rejected.why: Wrong attachment of 'for your sake': 'διὰ σὲ' goes with 'λαβεῖν ἐκ σοῦ' (to take from you for your sake), not with the whole clause as a parenthetical. The English makes 'for your sake' seem like a general beneficence, but Greek specifies 'to take [form] from you for your sake.' Also 'without corruption' should attach to the taking, not float at the end.
last_rejected.fix: who for your sake was pleased to take the form of a servant from you without corruption
last_rejected.ruling: English 'take...from you...for your sake' captures διὰ σὲ with λαβεῖν ἐκ σοῦ; 'without corruption' attaches to taking. No error.

last_rejected.quote: the Father comes to dwell with you
last_rejected.why: Wrong sense: 'ἐπιδημεῖ' means 'visits, comes to stay as a visitor, sojourns,' not 'comes to dwell with' which implies permanent residence. The Father's 'visitation' is temporary and gracious, not co-residence.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Comes to dwell with' is within range of ἐπιδημεῖ (sojourn/visit/dwell). Mere preference.

last_rejected.quote: Do not doubt as you seat in a manger
last_rejected.why: Wrong agency: Mary is not actively 'seating' Christ in the manger; she is giving birth and the context implies placing or the passive result. 'καθίζουσα' here is circumstantial—'as [He] is seated' or 'as you place [Him].' But 'seat' as transitive with Mary as subject overstates her agency; the Greek is more about her being in the situation where He is placed.
last_rejected.fix: Do not doubt as in a manger He is placed
last_rejected.ruling: καθίζουσα is circumstantial participle; 'as you seat' is a reasonable rendering. Mere preference.

last_rejected.quote: so that like cattle they may run up thinking to find handfuls of barley in the manger—and may eat the true bread
last_rejected.source_quote: ἵνα ὡς κτήνη προσδράμωσι δράγματα κριθῆς ἐπὶ τῆς φάτνης εὑρεῖν οἰόμενοι καὶ τὸν ἄρτον τὸν ἀληθινὸν φάγωσι
last_rejected.why: Wrong syntax: 'οἰόμενοι' goes with 'thinking to find handfuls of barley,' but the English 'run up thinking to find...and may eat' breaks the construction. The Greek has them running up thinking to find barley handfuls, AND [then] eating the true bread. The English 'and may eat' after the dash makes 'may' carry over, but 'thinking' wrongly attaches to 'run up' rather than to the purpose of finding. The structure is: run up (thinking to find barley) → and eat true bread. The English obscures that they don't find what they seek but something better.
last_rejected.fix: so that like cattle they may run up, thinking to find handfuls of barley in the manger, and may eat the true bread
last_rejected.ruling: English preserves the contrast: thinking to find barley but eating true bread. No meaning changed or lost.
